To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Nonlinear piezoresistive and piezoelectric behavior in flexural harvesters is strongly influenced by the presence of proof mass, and 2) the presence of proof masses precipitates nonlinear resonances at lower base excitation levels, while increasing the influence higher-order nonlinearities, which can be successfully modeled with nonlinear damping and elastic constitutive relations.

nonlinear nonconservative piezoelasticity is a suitable modeling approach for nonlinear piezoelectric harvesters, and that the addition of successsively larger proof masses to piezoelectric cantilevers results in the precipitation of nonlinear resonances at lower drive amplitudes and the increase of higher-order nonlinear effects.

the addition of a proof mass to a cantilever beam energy harvester increases the amplitude of nonlinear effects and that the nonlinearities are primarily due to material properties rather than the piezoelectric coupling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a nonlinear nonconservative piezoelastic constitutive model for the analysis of the piezoelectric vibration energy harvester.
the development of nonlinear piezoelectric modeling for piezoelectric cantilever energy harvesters.
the nonlinear nonconservative behavior of a piezoelectric cantilevered beam subjected to base excitation and a proof mass.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nonlinear piezoelectric model is a good model for the piezoelectric system.

nonlinear nonconservative behavior is a significant factor in the performance of piezoelectrical energy harvesters and that a nonlinear model is needed to accurately predict their performance in a variety of applications.
the addition of proof mass increases the influence of higher order nonlinearities and that the use of nonlinear constitutive relations is preferred over the use of nonlinear damping.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the nonlinearities in a piezoelectric cantilever energy harvester can be modeled with a single-degree-of-freedom nonlinear model with linear piezoelectric coupling, and the model can predict the frequency response and the power output of the energy harvester.
a nonlinear model is needed for the design and optimization of energy harvesting devices when the base excitation is weak.
the nonlinear behavior of a PZT-actuated cantilever beam is dominated by nonlinear elastic and damping effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple nonlinear damping model can capture the observed nonlinear behavior of piezoelectrics.
a nonlinear model is needed when the drive amplitude exceeds the linear regime.
the use of a linear piezoelectric model is adequate for predicting the frequency response of a piezoelectric cantilever for a wide range of excitation amplitudes.
